utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Would the Registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-03-67-R77.3, the Prosecutor versus Vojislav Seselj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I have the appearances. Before that, Mr. Seselj, I wanted to make sure that you are following the proceedings in the language you understand. Do you receive the interpretation into your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can follow the proceedings only in the Serbian language. Right now I am receiving interpretation into Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Seselj. Then can I have the appearances. Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. My name is Bruce MacFarlane. I'm an attorney from Canada and have been appointed as the amicus curiae Prosecutor in these proceedings. To my right is Ms. Lori Ann Wanlin, who is with me this morning and has been with me throughout the proceedings. She is also a member of the Canadian bar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacFarlane. Welcome, Ms. Wanlin. Mr. Seselj, if you could introduce yourself for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dr. Vojislav Seselj, university Professor and the greatest enemy of The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Seselj. As the Chamber indicated in its Scheduling Order of 28th January, 2011, the trial in these proceedings will start today. However, before we start, there are a few matters that we need to deal with in the Pre-Trial Conference. First, I'd like to deal with the amicus Prosecutor's oral request for right of audience of Ms. Lori Ann Wanlin. And during the Status Conference held on 14th December last year, the amicus Prosecutor requested that his legal assistant, Ms. Wanlin, be granted a limited right of audience in these proceedings in that she would be allowed to participate in the presentation of evidence, cross-examination, and representation or argument under his supervision. The accused opposed this request. On 16th February, 2011, the Chamber informally notified the parties that the amicus Prosecutor's request was granted to the extent, however, that this decision would not have any financial implication for the Registry. We hereby reiterate that position. Next, the Chamber wishes to deal with the amicus Prosecutor's bar table motion. On 17th January this year, the amicus curiae Prosecutor filed the confidential Prosecutor motion for admission of evidence from the bar table in which the amicus Prosecutor seeks the admission of 72 exhibits which can be grouped into the following four categories: First, documents forming part of the official court record in the cases case number IT-03-67-T, IT-03-67-R77.2, and IT-0367-R77.3; secondly, evidence related to the book which is the subject of these proceedings; thirdly, 13 procès-verbal; and finally, fourthly, a series of screen shots showing the accused's website. Mr. Seselj did not file a response within the dead-line set forth in Rules 126 bis of the Tribunal's rules, which expired on 10th of February. Having reviewed the material proposed for admission, the Chamber is of the view that it is relevant and of probative value and thus satisfy the requirements of Rule 89(C), and therefore the Chamber will admit it into evidence. The Chamber requests that Registry assign the appropriate exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection, Mr. Kwon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, I am not, I am not opposed to having these documents admitted into evidence. However, in the last request made by Mr. MacFarlane, what has presented are excerpts from my Internet website and even the front page of my latest book. I think that that is improper; namely, that the amicus Prosecutor had to obtain the original of the book and that that would have been conscientious on his part. Since he did not obtain the book and since you have just admitted it into evidence, I am offering a copy of that book to the Trial Chamber, and to Mr. MacFarlane and his associate another copy, and then the entire book can be admitted into evidence. As for Mr. MacFarlane and his associate, perhaps I can write a dedication for them during the break because the title of the book contains his name. So could you please instruct the usher to take these two copies, along with my proposal to have this admitted into evidence, so that it is a serious piece of evidence, not so unserious [as interpreted] as presented by Mr. MacFarlane. And I have two copies for the prosecuting side.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Seselj. We'll see whether we need to admit the original book, and it is always welcome for the parties to co-operate with each other on a voluntary basis. Next we are going to deal with the amicus Prosecutor's motion dated 21st of February entitled, "Original Motion to Amend the Rule 65 ter E 3 Exhibit List." Here, my understanding is that the amicus Prosecutor seeks to add documents related to the accused's recent publication of confidential information, documents that reflect a pattern of changing service providers and website registrants, and the English translation of excerpts from documents already on the original 65 ter exhibit list. Mr. MacFarlane, I take it that the accused hasn't received the B/C/S translation of this motion, so the thing may be that the accused is not in the position to respond to this. But having said that, on a separate note, could you expand on the reason why we have to -- we need --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have received that, Mr. Kwon. I have received that, as far as I can remember, and I can respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In your language and you can respond?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the most beautiful Serbian language, Mr. Kwon. It's already been two years now that the Registry of The Hague Tribunal has been trying to do away with my Internet website by sending instructions to these distributors of the Internet in Sweden, Germany, Serbia, and they haven't succeeded in doing that throughout those two years. They succeeded in the beginning of February this year; however, six hours later, my website appeared elsewhere. It proved to be indestructible. Secondly, at my proposal, the appropriate authorities of the Serb Radical Party appointed my oldest son, Nikola Seselj, to be editor of my website, since in that case I am quite sure that he is not going to relent to any kind of pressure and that I'm going to be the main creator of the website and that nobody is going to intimidate him in order to remove anything from my website. What I decide once and for all to have on my website remains there. Once and for all. And no one can do away with that. You can find a new distribute yet again. The one where my website is now, perhaps you can force them to do away with my website. I'm going to find another one and yet another and so on and so forth. And if I do not manage to do that, then I'm going to address my great friend, the great leader of the Korean people, Kim Jong-il to re-establish my website. And no one can force him to relent to any kind of pressure exerted by The Hague Tribunal. So my website will not be destroyed. Then there's my friend Hugo Chavez, then there's my friend Mahmoud Ahmadinejad. I have friends throughout the world and I will find friends throughout the world who are going to take good care of my website and will not allow you to do away with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, in a nutshell, you are not opposed to that motion?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've already said that to you in my last motion. As far as I can remember, Mr. MacFarlane provided a photograph of the cover page of the book taken from the website. However, I am providing additional information to you, that I have made sure that no one can destroy my website. You can kill me, but you cannot destroy my website. It has become indestructible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: However, Mr. MacFarlane, the Chamber is of the view that it would in the interest of justice and the judicial economy if we limit the scope or the focus of this trial to -- on the publication of his three books, on books revealing the identities of the protected 11 witnesses, and deferring all the other issue, i.e., the -- whether he should comply with the Court Order to remove some certain confidential material from his website, to a certain and later stage, given that there are several pending matters before the Chamber in relation to those matters. So what do you think about that approach?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Perhaps I could respond by outlining what animated me to proceed in this fashion and then the Chamber can consider that. In the Chamber's decision of the 2nd of December --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we do remember. In our decision to amend the indictment, we said at the end that the amicus curiae may consider such material as the aggravating circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes, and perhaps even more so that, to use the words of the Chamber, considering that for the purposes of the indictment the support of the book, namely whether it was available in hard copy or in electronic format or both, is immaterial to the central issues as whether or not the witness's identities are revealed in the said book. And so it struck me that the format was irrelevant. The question was whether or not the 11 witnesses were identified improperly, or any number of the 11 witnesses. And this most recent book that emerged in the last few weeks, it seemed to be compounded, the situation, and formed a part of an overall transaction that has lasted for quite some time. And that for the purposes of judicial economy, to collapse everything into one proceeding, because it all related to the same witnesses, made sense to me. And that was in essence what animated me to seek to include it as a compounding of the contempt and as a continuation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I say something else before you make a decision. Judges, the amicus curiae would have to bear in mind some certain facts. Elementary facts. He has to appear in court in a serious fashion. He cannot say that this book was published a few days ago. He has to know the exact date when the book was published. The book was published during the last days of December last year. That can be established by checking it at the printing press and checking in the National Library of Serbia where the first printed copies of any publication are sent first and foremost. So it wasn't a few days ago. It was at the end of December last year. The book was published immediately after I filed, according to Rule 65 ter, the list of witnesses that I intend to call during the course of these proceedings. And the statements of these witnesses are contained in that book. Each and every one of these witnesses is saying that he or she is giving this statement publicly, that they agree to have it published, and so on. I did not publish any statement given to the Prosecution earlier on by any one of these witnesses. I am just publishing their public statements. And every one of them signed before a notary their consent to have the statement published. Mr. MacFarlane doesn't know that because the book hasn't been translated for him. He didn't make an effort to obtain the book. He didn't even find out when it was printed and how many copies and so on and so forth. That is not serious. There's a look of seriousness there. He is using a lot of UN money but he is not doing his job conscientiously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As I indicated, Mr. MacFarlane, the Chamber is of the view to limit the scope of this case to the sole issue whether he violated the order of the Court by publishing that book in a way of revealing the identity and the protected statements of those protected witnesses. So what we are going to allow to add to the list is the -- those English translation of excerpts from documents already on the original 65 ter exhibit list. And your intention is not only to add them to the list, but also to tender them for those documents to be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, Your Honours. I do seek to tender those documents. And as well, there is a further issue concerning the report that parties and the Chamber received yesterday from the Registrar. It touches on issues in relation to the former book. And for that reason I would seek to tender that and to file an amended 65 ter list as well. It's my submission that it's directly relevant -- in the event of finding of guilty to the current count, it's directly relevant to the question of sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is not quite sure whether it is necessary to admit it for the purpose of this case, so we leave it as it is. Mr. Seselj, we come to your motion to call your character witnesses. On 28th January, 2011, Mr. Seselj submitted a list of 28, I quote, "character witnesses," whom he stated should be called at trial to testify to his good character and the context in which his books have originated. The motion was filed confidentially upon order of the Chamber as it contained information which remained still confidential. The Chamber wishes to remind Mr. Seselj that Rule 46 of the Tribunal's rules on misconduct of counsel is also applicable to self-represented accused. This list of character witnesses contains abusive and insulting languages and suits no other purpose than to obstruct the trial process and make a mockery of the Tribunal and these proceedings in particular. The Chamber therefore dismisses the list of character witnesses as frivolous and an abuse of process. I think this disposes of the pending matters. Now we turn to the planning of this trial. So I -- Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Mr. Kwon, not all pending matters have been resolved yet. First of all, as regards my motion that you rejected, it does not contain a single insulting or derogatory term. It just contains the titles of book published long ago that may be considered derogatory but are -- but cannot be changed as such, so in the original they have to be there. I mean, there are no other things that may be deemed improper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Seselj, the Chamber has given its ruling already. So, Mr. MacFarlane, how long do you expect your Prosecution case to last?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I can confirm that I do not intend to call any viva voce evidence. I do intend to tender the documents that have been received. And in terms of length of time, I can confirm that I expect it will still be between three and five hours, probably closer to four, but that's just my best assessment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you planning to make an opening statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you will make closing argument after having concluded all the evidence including Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. When I say between three to five hours, that includes the opening statement. So it's the -- my proposal and my submission is that we could proceed along these lines, consistent with previous contempt cases in which I was involved: I would provide an opening statement which would provide the usual overview of the evidence, the documents would then be tendered in a more formal way with comments on the relevance of each document for the benefit of the Chamber, and that would bring us pretty well close to the end of the case for the Prosecution. But all of that, what I just described, would be between three and four hours, I suspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacFarlane. Mr. Seselj, the Chamber has been informed by the pro se liaison office that there may be issues concerning the scheduling of your ten witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know what this word conflict means to you right now. There's no conflict. I wish to present ten Defence witnesses, and I submitted all the filings very properly, I provided their preliminary statements, they have been translated into the English language. However, the Registry made it impossible for me to meet with my associates, with my Legal Advisor, Dejan Mirovic, who has a master's degree in law, and another associate of mine, Nemanja Sarovic, who also has a degree in law. I submitted a request last year, towards the end of last year, that they come and visit me and that the Registry pay for their travel expenses. They visited me once before, however, the Registry did not allow Nemanja Sarovic a privileged visit. And then Dejan Mirovic, by way of a demonstration, refused to come. My Legal Advisor and Case Manager have not visited me at all since this indictment was issued. On the 17th of February, I received a letter from Jaimee Campbell, head of the department of OLAD, and she says that the Registry is not going to pay travel expenses at all for my Legal Advisor and the Case Manager. I hope that you have a copy of that letter. If not, I have a copy in the English language and you can take it if you're interested in seeing it. So I did not manage to prepare thoroughly with these proceedings because I did not have a single meeting with my Legal Advisor and the Case Manager. Secondly, I would have to proof the witnesses. My plan was an examination in chief of about half an hour of each witness, so that means about five hours altogether for the examination-in-chief. However, I have to talk to every one of the witnesses before they walk into the courtroom. That is the practice of The Hague Tribunal, that all witnesses are proofed regardless of whether they are Prosecution witnesses or Defence witnesses. I have to proof these witnesses and I have no possibility of doing so. The Registrar is standing in my way. I don't have enough money to pay for everyone's travel expenses. This is something that should be covered by the Tribunal. This is not financing my Defence as such. Covering travel expenses in each and every trial is not something that is a bank roll by the Defence's budget. It has to be financed by the Registry and cannot be charged to the Defence. In my trial, the financing of my Defence has not been resolved yet. We need to cover the travel expenses and the accommodation expenses for one Legal Assistant, one Case Manager, and then a total of ten witnesses that I'm calling. At the outset you told us that this exceptionally nice lady whose assistance Mr. MacFarlane has enlisted for this trial is in a position to address the Trial Chamber. And then it strikes me that I don't have a single assistant of any kind who will have an opportunity to address the Court or not. We need to be on an equal footing here. The Tribunal is paying Mr. MacFarlane and his associate and God knows who else. Well then I say the Tribunal should pay for my associates too. The financing of my Defence has not been resolved yet, but at least the Tribunal needs to cover their travel expenses so that they could be here and help me along with my Defence and proofing the witnesses. I call some witness. All these witnesses are persons who have something to do with the charges against me, in terms of publishing certain names, with the exception of one person whose name I will not mention now, it is a witness who was established as committing perjury a long time ago. Last year the Prosecutor informed me and the Trial Chamber in writing that they will not be invoking the testimony of that witness at all. Even the Prosecutor believes, is convinced, that the testimony was false. That is why I have no need at all for that witness. Nevertheless, as for the remaining ten witness, levelling serious accusations against the OTP, are truly indispensable. Indispensable why? I need them here in this courtroom to confirm that their names were published by their own free will. It wasn't something I did without their consent. I was merely the person who made it happen. Not a single confidential document containing their names was published that was disclosed to me by the OTP. The only documents published were the documents that were created while my associates were interviewing those witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, in short, you are not in the position to proceed with your Defence case, given the reasons you stated. So, Mr. Seselj, going back to that financing issue, as you are well aware by now, matters relating to the financing of the -- of an accused's Defence are within the primary responsibility of the Registrar. It is unfortunate that this financing issue could not be resolved before today and that it will delay the completion of these proceedings, which could and should have been completed in a relatively short time-frame. However, the Chamber cannot but adjourn the proceedings since the Chamber is of the view that you are entitled, under Article 21.4(e) of the Statute, to obtain the attendance and examination of witnesses on your behalf under the same conditions as witnesses against you. The Chamber would note, however, that as a self-represented accused, Mr. Seselj, you are responsible for making the initial preparation to secure the prompt attendance of your witnesses. The pro se liaison office without doubt will provide you with all the necessary assistance you may need in this respect. And also in order to get financing assistance from the Registry as an indigent person, there are certain procedures you have to take. That's all we can say at this moment, Mr. Seselj. In order not to waste time, the Chamber considers that the amicus Prosecutor would present his case today and that the proceedings should be adjourned sine die thereafter, pending the resolution of the accused's Defence by the Appeals Chamber. And the parties will be informed in writing as to the date of recommencement of trial and how long Mr. Seselj will be granted for the presentation of the case. The Chamber's Legal Officer will contact the amicus curia Prosecutor as well as Defence via pro se liaison office. Yes, Mr. MacFarlane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you for the ruling. I just wanted to reiterate a point that I made before Judge Hall on the last Pre-Trial Conference, just so that there's no -- no one's taken by surprise. I did want to mention on the last occasion that I will be quite a distance from Northern Europe for a period of time in April and early May and I just wanted to note that. I'm quite happy to work with the Senior Legal Officer in terms of working out a date, but I wanted to be fair to the Chamber and let you know in advance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. MacFarlane. The Chamber is cognizant of that information. Then, Mr. MacFarlane, you have the floor. The first break will be at 20 past 10.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I expect that I will in all likelihood be completed by the time of the break. I will endeavour to do that. These proceedings arise by virtue of Rule 77 of the Rules of this Tribunal, which in essence provides that the Tribunal in the exercise of its inherent power may hold in contempt those who disclose information in knowing violation of an order of the Chamber. The -- on a review of the Order in Lieu of Indictment, there are -- and in light of the evidence that I will be alluding to, there are really two aspects to this case that I would like to highlight at the beginning. The first relates to a hard cover book which contained confidential information. And the second aspect relates to the inclusion of that same book and confidential information on the personal website of the accused. And we've already discussed briefly the effect and impact of the decision of this Chamber on the 2nd of December, which noted that there was no need to amend the Order in Lieu of Indictment but, rather, all of those matters could be dealt with under the general rubric of the current Order in Lieu of Indictment. So as a result, during the course of the presentation of the Prosecution's evidence, you will hear evidence on both of those aspects of the case. The facts in this case, in my respectful submission, are actually quite straightforward. The foundation of the case rests on several orders of Chambers. There were two orders at an early stage which are all embracing in connection with these proceedings and are nonspecific to individual witnesses. The first was issued by Trial Chamber II in 2003, and that focused on the importance of confidentiality of disclosure. The second, likewise, was a decision of Trial Chamber II in 2004, and that focused once again on the confidentiality of disclosure materials. So the general framework for these proceedings and the importance of confidentiality was established at an early stage, and the evidence will demonstrate that the accused was present throughout the proceedings and was aware of both of those general orders. Subsequently, however, the Trial Chamber ordered various protective measures that were specific to the 11 witnesses in issue. Those three orders emerged in June of 2005, August of 2007, and October of 2007. I won't go into the details too much of these because I want to be careful in terms of not disclosing any confidentiality myself, so I will endeavour to be general. In connection with the 2005 order, the order was issued unanimously and granted protective measures in connection with a number of witnesses who are named and who were assigned a pseudonym. In connection with the second order in August of 2007, that matter was conducted and emerged from the Pre-Trial Judge who gave a very detailed set of protective measures. And the evidence will demonstrate before you the lengths to which the Pre-Trial Judge considered the witnesses on an individual basis and evidence concerning those individual witnesses. And then in a very tailored way, tailored a series of protective measures that was responsive to the circumstances concerning each of those witnesses. And in the third and final order of protective measures in October of 2007, once again before the Pre-Trial Judge, there was a further consideration again on an individualized basis with particular attention to the evidence that was provided to the Pre-Trial Judge. And once again there is a carefully-tailored set of protective measures that was prepared and ordered by that Chamber. The point of all of that is simply that in the tradition of the Chambers at the International Tribunal, there is very careful attention to the evidence and a tailoring of the protective measures to respond to the evidence and that the accused was aware of that and was present and received copies of the orders. The position that we're in, then, as of late 2007 after the completion of all of these orders was that specific protective measures were in place for all 11 witnesses that are in issue in these proceedings. The evidence will demonstrate through a series of decisions procès-verbal and submissions from the accused that he was aware that these protective measures were in place. And more particularly, the evidence will demonstrate that he knew that there was a prohibition on the publishing of information in connection with these protected witnesses. It will also be demonstrated through the evidence that the accused was very much aware of the fact that there was a need to come back to Chambers if there's a desire to rescind or vary this detailed framework of protective measures. The evidence on that will be quite overwhelming. So, moving forward a little bit to late 2007, just to summarise what the evidence will demonstrate: It will demonstrate that protective measures were in place, they have been fully considered by the Chamber, the accused knew that they were in place, the accused knew he couldn't publish confidential information that fell within the framework that had been established by Chambers, and he knew that he couldn't publish confidential submissions. Moving from late 2007 until around the middle of 2008, slightly beyond the middle of 2008, the evidence will demonstrate a fair bit of activity on the part of the accused in terms of this whole protected witness framework. The accused became somewhat litigious during this period of time on this issue. And through his submissions and decisions that emerged, it will demonstrate quite clearly in terms of the accused's knowledge that the accused knew that Chambers, and not he and not other third parties, but Chambers controls the process of determining whether protective measures are issued and whether they are rescinded and whether they're varied. The evidence will demonstrate, and this is important in the overall scheme, that the accused knew that it was necessary, if there was a desire to rescind or vary, that one needs to proceed back to Chambers so that there can be a judicial assessment of whether that's an appropriate step. And in fact, the evidence will demonstrate that the accused and his associates actually assisted one individual in going back to Chambers. Further to that, during this, what I'll refer to as a litigious period, the accused himself brought a motion for protective measures in respect of certain witnesses. So it's quite clear in terms of the accused's knowledge, he had a fairly, not a fairly, a pretty good understanding of the statute and the rules and the procedures that were necessary. And that will certainly be an inference that will be open to the Chamber upon full consideration of the evidence. So now, in terms of moving forward and the position that we're in right now, the orders are in place, the accused is familiar with the legal scheme and the framework. The evidence will in the next stages, as we move along in this continuum, will demonstrate his breaches. And the evidence will show that those breaches of the order and the scheme that was in place was done knowingly, was deliberate. And I anticipate the evidence will demonstrate that he was defiant in his approach. And that, in my respectful submission, is exactly what the contempt scheme is intended to deal with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MACFARLANE
utterances.text: (redacted). First of all, it disclosed information that enabled the reader to identify the protected witnesses by publishing their full names, publishing their addresses, and publishing in most instances their identity card number. So the information was quite specific. And on some of the witnesses, not all necessarily, but in several instances, the breaches went further and outlined such identifying information as dates of birth, place of birth, occupation, and unique master citizen number. I anticipate that the evidence will demonstrate that this is not a case where the information that was published simply tends to identify or is capable of identifying or may identify protected witnesses. This is a case of actual identification of persons who are were still under a protective legal umbrella. But the 2008 book actually goes further than that. There is a second dimension to the manner in which it breached the orders of protection. The book reprints submissions to the Tribunal that have been reclassified by Chambers as confidential and for reasons that were appropriate throughout. But I expect the evidence will demonstrate that these submissions which to the knowledge of the accused were confidential were deliberately published, and they in turn contained further identifying information. You will receive evidence demonstrating, in relation to these submissions, that they originated from the accused; they were reclassified as confidential by the Chamber in the normal course of events pursuant to internal protocols; that the accused knew of the reclassification through a formal notice process that's well-established within the Tribunal; and that the accused knew of the implications of publishing confidential information, including his own submissions that have been classified as confidential. Concerning the 2008 book, the evidence, I anticipate, will demonstrate beyond a reasonable doubt that the publication of this information was done deliberately and defiantly and was certainly not done accidently. The evidence will show that he was aware of the orders and decided to publish anyway. Concerning the scope of publication, which is always relevant in a case of publication contempt, the accused further compounded the contempt beyond simply publishing a book in hard cover. The hard cover book, the evidence will show, had a print run of approximately 10.000, but that contempt was compounded by publishing the book on his own website. I think, in my submission, the website aspect to the case is an important one for the Chamber to consider because if one, through normal hard cover books, seeks to distribute information, there are the normal limitations of getting the information out. You only have certain numbers of copies, each copy costs something, you need to promote it, you need to get it out. So there's all sorts of limitations to a hard cover book. But the decision to publish on the Internet was a very serious step. Internet publication is far more pervasive than print publication for a number of reasons. First of all, you have potentially a worldwide audience well beyond what a hard copy book to be directed to. Secondly, you have virtually an unlimited number of readers who could, as the evidence will demonstrate, download the book free of charge. Thirdly, the evidence will demonstrate that the book has been available on the website of the accused since the earlier portion of 2010, and the evidence will demonstrate that it's still on the Internet. Fourthly, and there's quite a number of points that can be made in terms of why the Internet publication is more serious, but the last one that I'll mention at this point is that in the case of a hard cover book there have been instances where the book was recalled, and I have personally been involved in instances of that. Where the book or the information is on the Internet is virtually impossible to do any sort of effective recall. I can draw my comments to a conclusion by simply summarising what I expect will be the thrust of the case for the Prosecution. As I have mentioned on a couple of occasions, in terms of the mens rea or fault requirement of the offence of contempt, I anticipate that the evidence will be very convincing, that this was a deliberate and defiant approach by the accused. The case, as I mentioned at the beginning, is relatively straightforward. Protective measures were in place, the accused was familiar with the scheme, he became litigious, he had been unsuccessful in his attempts to rescind. And it would be open to the Chamber to draw the inference that he arrived at a new strategy and that was to not simply go back to Chambers to have the protective measures dealt with in Chambers but, rather, to get the information out through other means, namely through the book and the website publication of the information he wanted to have public. The evidence will demonstrate that one of the objectives and one of the motives of the accused was that he wanted to ensure that the public would see the evidence that went before the Chamber, unobstructed and in full light. That was his overall objective on the basis of the evidence. He felt frustrated and adopted a new strategy. That's a rather brief outline of the case as I expect it will be presented to you by the Prosecution. Given the given the ruling of the Chamber with respect to the right of audience, for which I thank the Chamber, the next stage in the presentation --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your intervention is not helpful, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.text: As I was just about to say, the next stage in the case for the Prosecution will involve a presentation by my colleague with respect to the documentary evidence. utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. Precisely, Mr. Kwon. Precisely. Because I do know what the practice in the Tribunal is. utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.text: Let me be clear. Do we have a translation of transcript as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. WANLIN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We don't have the translation of the transcripts. One of the points that I was going to be making was to read out the sections of the transcripts and therefore the accused would receive the relevant sections in B/C/S so that he would be able to comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we don't have the translation of Court decisions, do we?

utterances.speaker: MS. WANLIN
utterances.text: I don't have the decisions in the binders. They are available on CD and this is where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There exist English translation of -- B/C/S translation of Court decisions?

utterances.speaker: MS. WANLIN
utterances.text: Yes, the B/C/S versions do exist. And I will point out that the procès-verbal are actually in both B/C/S and in English, as are -- several of the exhibits I'll be referring to are in both B/C/S and in English. And further, many of the documents are actually English translations of the accused's book and therefore we don't have the B/C/S copy.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, Mr. Kwon, I insist that I be given everything in the Serbian language. The transcripts must be submitted to me in the Serbian language. It is simply not practicable for Mrs. - I can't seem to remember her name - read back portions of the transcript and then to have that orally interpreted to me. utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: These transcripts are part of the transcript which pertains to the trial against Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: MS. WANLIN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given that these are part of the trial of Mr. Seselj and he has access to the video, audio/video file, the Chamber will proceed with the presentation of evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, Mr. Kwon, not only did I receive the recordings of those trial, I was actually in the courtroom myself, but the transcript from my trial runs into over 20.000 pages of typed up text. Over 20.000 pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber has given its ruling. Let's proceed, Ms. Wanlin.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, probably the best thing would be for the Trial Chamber to decide to press on with this case against me, if you intend to keep me here as a passive observer. You are violating my rights openly, brutally. You are telling me the Chamber has given its ruling. What's my role then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your intervention is not helpful, Mr. Seselj. We'll see to it that your rights are protected to the full extent. Let's proceed, Ms. Wanlin.

utterances.speaker: MS. WANLIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like to have the assistance of the Court Usher if possible. I will be referring to a document on the ELMO system. This is a revised document that you have already received in the pre-trial brief. And if you look in your binders, a copy of it is in the front of the -- Sorry, please, this should be -- this is confidential, so if it could be broadcast to the Chamber and not to the audience, that would be recommended, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would it be of any use to you, Mr. Kwon, if I told you that this document is only in the English language? There is nothing whatsoever in it that is in the Serbian language. Is that any use to you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is not an exhibit. This is just aid. Let's see what we can get from this. Yes, Ms. Wanlin.

utterances.speaker: MS. WANLIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. So I'll be beginning with three key questions that we'd like to address. The first was, was there a disclosure; the next is, were there protective measures in effect at the time of the disclosure; and thirdly, the question of did the accused have knowledge of the protective measures at the time of the disclosure. I will follow that with the evidence related to sentencing. The first question that I will address is: Were there orders of a Chamber in effect at the time --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Thank you for slowing down.

utterances.speaker: MS. WANLIN
utterances.text: My apologies. Were there orders of a Chamber in effect at the time of the disclosure. I will draw your attention to Annex B, which is now on the ELMO system. Yes. And as you will note at the top of this diagram, it's a time-line. What we seek to establish is the point of publication in relation to when the protective measures were in effect and when there were submissions by the accused which were ordered confidential. You will note at the top we refer to the hard copy of the book was published. We've established that it was published after the 1st of September of 2008. The inside cover of the book does not specify the specific month of the publication. It merely refers to the year of publication. But there is a reference to -- in the book. I will refer you to tab 55 L.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: MS. WANLIN

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry, it has only --

utterances.speaker: MS. WANLIN
utterances.text: Pardon me, that was me misreading my notes. Tab I. Your Honours, I believe that there's a sticky note at the relevant section at the bottom of the page. And in light of the fact that we are in open session, I will simply refer to an interview that is noted on the particular date that -- in the publication by the name of "Vesti" which refers to an interview that was done by Nebojsa Stojanovic. I would now like to draw your attention to tab 56 which I will note is actually in B/C/S. And "Vesti," from our understanding, is a publication that is for the diaspora, it is published in a number of different places, but we can -- if we look at this second page, the back of the second page has the relevant parts translated, and this coincides with the information that was referred to at tab 55 I at the bottom of the page that I just referred to. So we believe that this helps to pin-point the date of publication. In addition to this, we would like to refer to, if you turn to tab 55 A, and on page 7, which once again is tabbed in Your Honours' binders, about partway down, there is a reference to a decision of the Chamber. I might ask to go momentarily into closed session, if I might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, I note the time. How about taking a break now. We'll have a break for half an hour and resume at ten to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, there is another problem that has cropped up which I would like to present to you before the lady continues. You allowed the Prosecutor to have an opening statement, nevertheless it is my impression that the lady from the Prosecution has already started presenting evidence. Under Rule 84 bis, I have the right following the opening statement of the OTP to make a statement in my capacity as an accused. It is not before such time that the Prosecution can go ahead and start presenting evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My apologies, I forgot to ask. I was minded to ask that but I just simply missed it. But is it your case that you want to make a statement based upon Rule 84 bis or Rule 84?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Under Rule 84, once the conditions are there. But all what I can do now is make an 84 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That was my question, whether you are minded to make a Rule 84 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long will that take?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, half an hour, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My apologies, Ms. Wanlin, for your inconvenience, but we'll proceed to hear Mr. Seselj's Rule 84 bis statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, judges. Do I have half an hour? Do I? I hope so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sirs, Judges, this is the second contempt proceedings against me at this Tribunal already. Why has the situation occurred? What has led to these proceedings? Because for eight years a Prosecutor has in vein been trying to create some kind of link between me and war crimes. The Prosecutor has suffered a fiasco. And what they are trying to do now is to use my time in detention which can in no way be justified and fill it with judgements and sentences for contempt of court. All that I have tried to achieve in this trial is to keep the public as well informed as possible of everything that goes on here. My right to a public trial is guaranteed under a great number of international conventions. These conventions say exactly when the nature of the trial can cease to be public. I will use a document which my Legal Associate Dejan Mirovic, MA in law, sent to the Security Council of the UN pursuant to my instructions in which he put forward a number of arguments about why trials that are not public run counter to fundamental human rights and freedoms. I can provide a copy in Russian, French, and English of this text in its entirety. Therefore, may copies please be made for the OTP as well, since I only happen to have a single copy on me right now. So could the Registry please use my copy to make copies both for the Trial Chamber and for the OTP. The European convention on the protection of human rights and fundamental freedoms guarantees that every human being has a right to a public trial. The public can only be shut out from this entire process only if the best interest of morale, the social structure, and constitution are best served or if there's a need to protect the interest of any minors involved or the public lives of any of the persons involved. I'm not being tried here for any sort of sexual offence. I'm not being tried for anything at all that might violate the moral order or the public order of democratic states. I stand accused here of the gravest of all crimes, crimes against humanity, before an international tribunal for war crimes. The crimes that we are talking about are exceptionally serious and the proceedings must be public in their entirety. Regardless of that, the Judges of The Hague Tribunal introduced Rule 77, allowing for the possibility to prosecute for contempt of court if information is published regarding protected witnesses. This rule has no foundation in international customary criminal law. This is something that the Judges of The Hague Tribunal came up with or invented. If you look at the statute of Rome, if you look at the rules, the statute of the ICC, you'll see that there is no provision about contempt of court there as defined by publishing names of protected witnesses. Needless to say, there are many witnesses who are in need of protection. Nevertheless, the protection is arranged before they appear in a courtroom and after they have left. Their appearance in a courtroom must be public. If there is any real danger involved, then the witness must be taken elsewhere far away, to the far end of the world, get their names changed, get their identities changed, give them the right conditions to get on with their lives, and so on and so forth. In my trial, there was absolutely no reason to have any witnesses at all protected in this way. I never threatened any of the witnesses. I never threatened to violate their physical integrity in any way. And these allegations are made in my trial. I never made a single threat to any of the witnesses. All I want to do is unmask false witnesses who appear in this courtroom and what I want to do is do this before the eyes of the public. Because if the public does not know what is happening during my trial, I might as well be swallowed by the earth beneath me. The public is the only form of protection that I enjoy and the only form of protection that I can count on. You know how many innocent people have been sentenced before this Tribunal over the last 18 years, starting with Milan Martic and then moving on to other innocent victims. These persons were perfectly innocent. Why were they sentenced? Because their Defence was inadequate and also because the public was shut out from parts of the proceedings. I enjoy the privilege of the Serbian national television broadcasting the entire trial, my entire trial, at least the public portions of my trial. And that had a particularly depressing effect on the OTP. The conspiracy at the outset that I should be sentenced in short order for purely political reasons, that has now failed. Mr. Kwon, exactly eight years ago you signed the first indictment against me. You were given some additional material but you did not take the trouble of studying that material because otherwise you would have seen that there was no serious evidence there and that the indictment was purely a political one. Carla del Ponte's book, which was published at a later date, clearly demonstrated why an indictment was raised against me. Why? Because at the time, I was in the way. I was in the way of the mafia pro-Western regime that was in power at the time. Zoran Djindjic, he clearly said, when he talked to Carla del Ponte, Take Seselj away and please don't ever send him back again. This policy continues. Now that you've taken him away, hold him there for as long as you can over there in The Hague. If you can't get him sentenced for crimes, war crimes, well, maybe you can get him sentenced for something else, contempt of court. How about that. For all I know there might be another ten trials where I will stand accused. I will certainly do my best to have at least another ten contempt trials instituted against me. I will not be deterred by anyone. As the great leader of all Korean people says, Kim Jong-il, Whoever fights sincerely in the interest of truth and freedom must be prepared to sacrifice, to make a sacrifice. I followed his shining example and I have demonstrated my readiness to make sacrifice, even if I should face death itself. Until my conditions are met and fulfilled, I will do my best to cope with whatever I may be subjected to here. I have since become indestructible and I will remain indestructible to the bitter end. Secondly, if we look at the codification of international criminal law - I've mentioned the statute, I've mentioned the rules of the ICC - it does not give you the right, it actually gives me the right in terms of contempt of court. If you look at the Rules on Procedure and Evidence, the statute of Rome, you have the following crimes clearly defined: Perjury. False testimony, no one has stood accused so far before this Tribunal for perjury, although there were instances of perjury and false witnesses in each and every trial here. Ask yourselves, Judges, why is that the case? You work as Judges in a Tribunal whose legality and legitimacy are entirely questionable. You have accepted your role but what you now must do is to defend your own honour and save face. What about infractions of moral standards and rules, basic human honesty and decency, what are the things happening here before this Tribunal. Many people managed to get away with many things, but I'm still hoping that at one point there will be a Judge who will put his foot down and say, That's enough. Hasn't happened yet, but I'm still hoping. It appears that I will yet see all of The Hague Tribunal's Judges appear in my case in various roles and guises, but I'm still hoping that there will be a Judge eventually who will put his foot down and say, My face is more important than the interests of the great political powers backing this Tribunal, particularly the US of A and the UK. This Tribunal is their political tool. This Tribunal was not set up to see to it that justice was done. If you look at the foundation documents of this Tribunal, it is defined as a tool for re-establishing peace, these so-called Pax Americana, and that is precisely what it continues to be. Justice is swept under the carpet. It's somewhere well concealed in the basement of this building. What we see surfacing more and more is the interests of the Western powers. In most other trials, I can't say all, but I can say most, and I've read every single judgement that has been made available to me, the Defence was instrumentalised by the Tribunal and fully paid by the Tribunal in most trials here. Whose interests did they represent? The payer's interests. Whoever was bank-rolling their work. There wasn't a single trial in which a Defence team was fully ready and prepared to oppose the wantonness of the Prosecutor or the respective Judges as the case may be. Mr. Kwon, you were a member of the Trial Chamber that tried Slobodan Milosevic. One of the witnesses appearing in the Milosevic trial was announced to be scheduled to appear in my trial; nevertheless, this particular witness appears to have changed his mind. The Tribunal failed to meet all of the promised conditions. So the witness simply changed sides. He said several times that he perjured himself in the Milosevic trial. He signed statements to that effect and addressed the issue publicly over in Serbia. He spoke to TV stations, to radio stations, and various newspapers in Serbia. This is O2C6 in my trial; that's the witness's code-name. I don't remember his code-name in the Milosevic trial, but he was the first witness who said, I was coerced into giving false testimony, and that is what I did, I gave false testimony. That should have rung the alarm bell throughout this Tribunal. I filed a criminal complaint with the president of the Tribunal. My complaint was thrown out and the explanation that followed was this: Proceedings are underway already to establish whether there are any elements to establish the responsibility of The Hague Tribunal for contempt, amicus curiae, who was appointed, whose name is being kept secret; it wasn't published, and I haven't been informed of that person's name, and now he would rise to the occasion. So this has been going on for over six months. My first criminal complaints were filed several years ago and the evidence was abundant, clearly indicating that there had been false testimony, that witnesses had coerced by the OTP to give false testimony, that they were made certain promises that turned out to be false. Or they were simply told that unless they testified as the OTP wanted them to testify, that they would be facing charges themselves. It was then said that no further indictments would follow after 2005. All the fear was suddenly gone. People started asking themselves certain questions and they started publishing certain facts, the truth. I have never published a single name of a false witness. No matter how false and no matter how persistent in their falsehood. All I did was to publish the testimonies of people whose hand was forced, who were coerced into giving false testimony. But at one point they turned around, they went back to the members of my Defence team, spoke to them, and gave statements that were entirely different and new. There were a total of about 20 such witnesses, many of them appearing in this courtroom as OTP witnesses, many of them appearing as the Chamber's witnesses. You will no doubt see that many of them were adamant that their testimonies should be public in their entirety, which eventually happened, their testimonies were public. One of them appeared in the courtroom, took a seat, and the Chamber told him that he would be testifying under protective measures, and he said, No way. The only way I can testify here is in public. There was a discussion in closed session for about an hour. The witness was adamant that his testimony should be a public one, and the Trial Chamber eventually ruled to drop this witness altogether. It took another 10 minutes for the Chamber after the decision was communicated to him to get the Trial Chamber to -- for the Trial Chamber to get the witness to leave the courtroom because he refused to go away. He wanted to testify. Many persons enjoy protective measures, but when they came to this courtroom it to testify, they openly said that they had never requested those measures. This was something that had been force upon them by the OTP against their own will and they decided to go ahead and testify in public. So I'm looking at a total of ten witnesses here whom I would like to bring here, and many of them have already as a matter of fact testified in public. I will give you the exact number. Most of them have testified in public. Four of them were eventually dropped by the Trial Chamber or by the OTP. Why did the OTP decide to drop certain witnesses and give up on their evidence? Because they were scared. If there is a witness who is adamant that he should testify in public, the whole conspiracy charge is gone and they can't get people to fabricate false testimonies. There was a lot of false evidence in the preliminary statements. The OTP never even tried to verify whether what was in those statements was feasible at all in terms of physically happening. One of the statements said that I had the Roman Catholic cathedral in Subotica blown up. But it's still there, alive and well, and no one ever blew it up. Maybe someone threw a fire cracker at one point or the other, but there wasn't even any serious material damage. There was certain witnesses who said that in my public speeches at rallies attended by several thousands of people I said that all children from mixed marriages should be killed. There was a witness who said there was this rally in August 1990 at Mali Zvornik and this witness claimed that the rally took place in March 1992. And then a link was established between that rally and the war events in Zvornik later on, but that was proved to be untrue. And yet nothing became of that. No one suffered any harm. In my trial, the OTP dropped two witnesses who were supposed to testify and who were here in the courtroom already, but then the OTP realised their testimonies were false, so they informed both me and the Trial Chamber that they would no longer be basing any of the charges on the evidence given by those witnesses. So what did I do? I stand accused of entirely fabricated crimes in Hrtkovci. I ordered my investigators to track down any documents available to counter the allegations of the OTP and to publish the whole thing in the form of a book. And then the Trial Chamber, headed by you, Mr. Kwon, sentenced me because a careful reader based on facts provided in the book on a number of different pages would have been led to the true identities of those witnesses. And I was sentenced to 15 months' imprisonment, which was far more severe than anyone had been punished previously for crimes of that nature. Earlier on there were cases where the witness's identities were made public in newspapers, on websites, and the sentences would be up to four months or maybe symbolic sums of money in the worst of cases. Two years ago you decided there was no reason to charge me about this book. That was at the same time when the proceedings were underway in relation to the other book, the hard-bound book that runs into 1.200 pages. And then what happens next, the Appeals Chamber sends this back to you, sends it back to the drawing board, and says, You have to try him for this book as well. So what do you do? You charge me. And then I wanted to have all of your rulings, the rulings that you made previously when you had decided to not charge me for that, but none were served on me. All of the rulings were served on the amicus curiae but I have not received any to this very day. Why would I need those? Well, Mr. Kwon, I need those to ascertain exactly your state of mind two years ago, at a point where you decided that there was no reason to press charges against me about that book. And yet now you have decided that there is reason to do just that. So what has changed in the meantime? I need to assess that. I can assess that based on your behaviour in the courtroom and any judgements that might follow. So what has happened in the mean time? It's got to be something strange. Two years ago there was no reason to go ahead with that. And now suddenly there is a sufficient reason to go ahead with the charges. Why now? Because in the meantime orders have come in from the Americans and the British that I should not be allowed to go back to Serbia until another round of parliamentary elections has run its course. Those were the orders. And the American and British servants over in Belgrade are adamant to see it done, those from the regime, those currently in power, and those masquerading as the opposition, obviously. It's not that I absolutely have to go back, not now, not ever, but I will not yield. I will not give way. What have I done? We have a total of 19 or 20 witnesses. These witnesses have decided to not appear as OTP witnesses but to make themselves available to the purpose of my Defence. They agreed to appear as Defence witnesses. I duly notified the Trial Chamber of the facts and I submitted their new statements. All of the previous rulings in the Trial Chamber were in reference to OTP documents. Protective measures were in relation to OTP witnesses and their preliminary statements. When those witnesses changed sides and decided to side with the Defence, suddenly they started speaking up in public. I'm this and that person, my name is this and that, the OTP wanted to force my hand and get me to appear in the trial against Vojislav Seselj, I was coerced, my hand was forced, or I was otherwise unaware of what I was signing, but I now refuse to appear as an OTP witness, and the testimony that is attributed to me is false, fabricated. I have never published a single statement given by any witness to the OTP. I've never published a single document that was under seal, that was placed under seal by the Trial Chamber. All I've ever published are statements made by those witnesses to me, those witnesses speaking up loud and clear for all the public to hear, telling the truth about any events that they may have been involved in, and particularly the truth about any events they were not involved in but their hand was forced by the OTP into giving false testimony about those same events. So that is what I have now done. And I made this public for all to see. What is the top-most interest of the public? The utmost interest of the public? To be informed. Have I imperilled everyone by informing the public that 20 Defence witnesses gave statements to me, although they had been Prosecution witnesses beforehand? And they agreed for me to disclose these statements publicly. I did not imperil anyone in that way, nor is it my intention to imperil anyone. My only intention is to unmask the OTP from The Hague. I wish I had been indicted earlier because then I would have shaken the foundations of the Tribunal already in 1995 or 1996 by showing the methods that the OTP has been using. I was indicted as a relatively late stage but I never gave up on my intention of doing that. I did that in this book. Now I published yet another book. Now, what did I present in that book? The only thing I presented were the statement of witnesses that I'm going to call here in this courtroom as Defence witnesses. They are all going to go through this courtroom and they are all going to testify in public. Every one of them gave me their consent in writing that I may disclose their statements as Defence witnesses publicly, and that is what I'm doing. Is there a court of law that can force these witnesses to remain anonymous? Especially since some of them had already testified in public in the main trial and they confirmed that they had never sought protective measures. They also confirmed that they had never been threatened. In different cases there were witnesses who, in order to get to a Western country and get a job there, home, money and so on, agreed to provide false testimony. There was a witness here who was haggling with the OTP just before he walked into the courtroom, whether he is going to testify in accordance with the statement that he gave to the OTP or the statement that he gave to me. He said that he would testify in favour of the Prosecution if they meet all his requests and if the OTP honours all its promises. This is one of the witnesses the OTP ultimately gave up on and they said that they would not base their charges on his statements. One witness claimed that he had been beaten up before arriving in The Hague by perpetrators unknown and then it was established that he was cleaning the snow somewhere and that he fell down some slippery steps. The Victims and Witnesses Unit here recorded his conversations with friends in Serbia. He called them and asked them to provide information to him stating that it was very dangerous for him there, that he was under a threat, so that he could somehow make The Hague Tribunal take care of him in a Western country, give him a job, a home, et cetera. Of course it's misery, poverty, that led him to do that kind of thing. When there is poverty, moral scruples become weaker, at least that's the case with most people but not all people. There are poor people who are ready to die but not sell out, not set out their virtue and honesty. There were people like that in The Hague as well, in The Hague Tribunal. Look at all the judgements that were passed on the basis of fabricated, trumped-up charges based on false witnesses. Starting with Milan Martic onwards. Remember the Milosevic case, Mr. Kwon. There were about 40 witnesses who denied the text of the preliminary statement they had given to the OTP. And remember that there was this one witness who claimed that the Serb police tried to execute him from a 10-metre distance using a heavy machine-gun. Four bullets were used and three grazed his shirt without hurting him. How can you remain unharmed if your shirt has exit/entry wounds? Slobodan Milosevic said, How come? And the witness said that God have saved him. You must remember that. You probably laughed about the whole thing with your colleagues later on because you couldn't laugh in court. It happened in other cases as well and no one reacted. Why was no one held responsible until now for perjury? Very soon I am going to file criminal charges against all the false witnesses in my case. Someone will have to be held accountable. What about Timothy McFadden? Why weren't criminal charges instituted against him on account of contempt of court? He disclosed to the American embassy information about the private life of Slobodan Milosevic. We don't know what WikiLeaks is going to leak out in the future. I hope that they are going to provide lots of documents that have something to do with me as well. The warden of the prison is telling the US embassy about Slobodan Milosevic's relations with his wife, with his friends, with his political colleagues, his daily activities, and so on. That is such a big time scandal that McFadden should have been in prison straightaway. He should have been punished. I filed a criminal complaint with the president of the Tribunal but I haven't received any response yet. It has been properly filed and translated into English. Why is the same yard-stick not applied to all? Why should McFadden be protected? Why should any Prosecutor from The Hague be protected? Why should perhaps even a Judge from The Hague be protected? While contempt proceedings are initiated against different journalists in most cases or people who refused to testify or in my very own case against an accused person. Just imagine a court of law in any part of the world. You all come from different countries. Imagine someone who has been charged with the gravest possible crimes, mass murder, terrible war crimes, and crimes against humanity. Instead of having intensive proceedings underway in court within a reasonable period of time, this person is charged in contempt proceedings on account of books that he published. You see how grotesque all of this is? That kind of grotesque thing cannot happen in any one of your countries, but it is possible before The Hague Tribunal. Because anything is possible here. The Rules of Procedure and Evidence have been changed 45 times and are being changed as proceedings are underway. When is this going to stop? When is this illegality and irregularity going to stop? Is it going to stop before the Tribunal closes down? Hardly. This Tribunal is going to be remembered in the history of International Law only by violating elementary legal regulations and human rights and freedoms. I spoke exactly for half an hour. I see that Mr. MacFarlane seems to be getting jittery, but it was exactly half an hour because I'm careful. I have thus concluded. Thank you.

What I can emphasise again is this: The matters related to the financing for the Defence are within the primary responsibility of the Registrar. There are procedures you have to follow in order to get that assistance. In the meantime, I hope the Appeals Chamber decision would resolve all the issues. On a practical matter, if we are to hear any evidence from the Defence witnesses, the only available date for the Chamber seems to be sometime at the end of May or in the beginning of June.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This year or next year? Is it this year you are talking about or next year?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That was a good one, Mr. Seselj.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything I say is good. Whatever I say goes down in the history of international legal science. If you were trying to intimidate me in this way and get me to give up my Defence altogether, then you have mis-assessed the situation. I will stick to my procedural rights. As far as I know, this might go on for another ten years, the trial that we are in the middle of right now. And the other trial might take another 20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next date for trial will be announced in due course to the parties. The hearing is now adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.16 p.m.
